acceptance: Candidate comparison is dated and binds official source/release identities, licenses, Node/React compatibility, and material operational tradeoffs.

The ADR selects one framework based on React 19 support, Node 24 compatibility, server/client boundaries, data/routing model, self-host portability, observability/tooling, security support, and repository alignment.
The selected exact framework version and React version produce a clean production build in a bounded qualification fixture.
The built candidate self-hosts on Node 24 and an HTTP request returns a deterministic expected marker.
No P01-S03 product shell or application feature is introduced.
Exact-head Ubuntu and Windows repository CI pass.

required: Official-source framework comparison with exact observed versions/revisions.
Selected-candidate production build and self-host HTTP smoke on Node 24.
ADR with explicit decision criteria, tradeoffs, and rejected alternatives.
Exact-head Ubuntu and Windows repository CI.

minimality.rationale: Use a disposable qualification fixture instead of introducing the real control-plane application before its dependency-ordered shell task.

requirements: Qualification fixture must not contain secrets, production endpoints, billing calls, or remote provisioning.
A framework marketing claim or prior planning preference is not acceptance evidence.

outcome: Select and prove the production React framework baseline for the Ineractive control plane using current official-source evidence and a reproducible build/self-host smoke, without prematurely building the product shell.
rationale: First P01 task after canonical P00 exit; downstream protocol and workspace work depends on a qualified framework baseline.

risk.recovery: Revert SG-000009, the qualification ADR/fixture/evidence, and selected-framework metadata; no external production side effect is authorized.

scope_in: Compare current production-grade React control-plane framework candidates using official-source version and capability evidence.
Evaluate Next.js App Router, React Router framework mode, and TanStack Start against Ineractive control-plane requirements.
Select one control-plane framework and record an ADR with explicit tradeoffs and rejected alternatives.
Create a bounded qualification fixture for the selected exact framework/React versions.
Execute deterministic build and self-host HTTP smoke evidence on the repository Node baseline.
scope_out: Do not build the real project/workspace shell; that remains IN-P01-S03-T01.
Do not change the generated-app compiler target merely because the control plane selects a framework.
Do not add Vercel-only or provider-only deployment assumptions.
